special_note: This card features Tom Brady in the uniform of the Montreal Expos, highlighting a unique aspect of his sports career.
description_block:
Graded GEM MT 10 by PSA (86713772). This is one of nine examples of this high-end piece recorded at its unimprovable tier in PSA's census reporting. This prestigious, essentially unimprovable Bowman Draft '95 Bowman Autographs Gold collectible displays record-setting NFL icon Tom Brady in the uniform of the Montreal Expos, who drafted him in the 18th round of the 1995 MLB Draft. Brady's blue ink on-card signature highlights the cardfront presentation. Since the first boxes of 2023 Bowman Draft baseball products hit shelves in November 2023, attention has been focused not on a young, top-ranked baseball prospect, but on the greatest quarterback the NFL has ever seen. This first-year insert set asks a simple question that could have changed the course of sporting history: what if Brady, a standout high school catcher, had chosen the diamond instead of the gridiron? Much to the rest of the NFL's dismay, Brady ultimately chose to attend the University of Michigan and play football instead of accepting the offer tendered by the Expos (prior to his 2022 retirement from the NFL, Brady was the last active athlete in any sport to be drafted by the Montreal franchise). An assured future Hall of Famer, Brady was a sixth-round selection by the New England Patriots in the 2000 NFL Draft. He is now generally considered the greatest football player in history, having led the Patriots to a staggering six Super Bowl victories; Brady added a seventh ring—more than any other player or individual franchise—in 2021 while quarterbacking the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. A captivating and attention-grabbing autographed insert piece, this exceptional cornerstone collectible was subject to a punishing jumbo pack-insertion rate of 1:26,639. Here's an exclusive, sterling showpiece from the most talked-about insert set of 2023. A statement on the card affirms the manufacturer's guarantee of authenticity for the piece's content and serves as the item's COA. The limited-edition piece is serial-numbered "40/50."

Featuring a black facsimile autograph on the obverse, this is the "Autografo" entry among the three Messi rookie cards available in the Barcelona-centric "Panini Sports Megacracks Barça Campeon" production. After a glittering European career that included 12 league titles, four UEFA Champions League crowns, and a record eight Ballons d'Or (as well as Copa América and FIFA World Cup titles for his home nation), Messi made the decision to take his talents to South Beach, setting up shop with MLS newcomers Inter Miami. Messi's stateside arrival has been nothing short of a phenomenon, garnering more attention than perhaps any other event in the history of American club soccer. The legend's performances—culminating in a 2025 MLS Cup title—have been front-page news in the United States, attracting new fans and widespread curiosity for MLS. The combination of the world's greatest-ever player and the world's largest media market has been a smash success for both parties and will continue to progress America's place in the club soccer landscape for years to come.

Bryant's 81-point outburst against the Raptors in 2006 and Curry's explosive performance against France in the gold medal game of the 2024 Summer Olympics are just two bullet points on an extensive list of blazing scoring performances. The two players are intrinsically tied by fearlessness and self-confidence, attributes that have allowed them to collect a combined nine NBA Finals titles, 29 All-Star Game selections, three league MVPs, and four scoring titles. Tragically, Bryant passed away in 2020 at the age of 41; he was elected to the Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame only four months later. special_note: This jersey was used in two games during the 2010-11 NBA season and is photo-matched to specific games.
description_block:
The NBA's all-time scoring king, LeBron James, used this Miami Heat home basketball jersey in two games during the 2010-11 NBA regular season, James' first season in South Beach after his highly publicized divorce from his hometown team, the Cleveland Cavaliers, which led into the iconic nationally-televised "The Decision." James first used this jersey on March 8, 2011, when he recorded a double-double with 31 points, a game-high 8 assists, and a game-high 11 rebounds in a 105-96 loss to the Portland Trail Blazers at Kaseya Center in Miami. He then used this jersey on March 12 in a 118-85 victory over the Memphis Grizzlies at Kaseya Center in Miami; James finished the game with 27 points, 5 assists, and 5 rebounds. Across both games, LeBron recorded a total of 58 points, 16 rebounds, and 13 assists. In his first season in Miami, "King James" led the Heat to their first of four consecutive NBA Finals appearances, an incredible dynastic run that resulted in two championship titles for Miami.
The offered jersey features all lettering and numbering in tackle twill. An NBA Logoman patch sits on the jersey's upper left chest, and the front left tail of the jersey contains an Adidas size "2XL" manufacturer's patch with an attached "LENGTH +2" flag adjacent to an "EVERY PLAYER. EVERY GAME." tag serial-numbered "MHE 00296." LOA from NBA/MeiGray (MHE00295) for game use for both games.
